outputs.L2: This application concerns the establishment of intrusion zones for security systems. In one example, a network device may retain information defining an intrusion zone for an audio/video (A/V) recording and communication device. The stored information may identify at least one condition applicable to the zone and at least one security-system response to be carried out when the A/V device detects movement in that zone and the specified condition is met. The network device may subsequently obtain motion information from the A/V device indicating that movement was detected within the intrusion zone. Upon receiving this information, the network device may determine—and make a further determination—that the zone’s conditional setting has been satisfied. In response to those determinations, the network device may direct the security system to execute the designated action or actions, such as triggering an alarm.
outputs.L3:
The application relates to the creation and management of intrusion zones within a security system. A network device stores intrusion-zone data associated with an audio/video recording and communication device, such as a security camera or video doorbell. The stored data defines the boundaries of an intrusion zone and includes one or more conditional settings, as well as actions to be performed when motion is detected within that zone and the specified conditions are met.

During operation, the network device receives motion data indicating that the audio/video recording and communication device has detected movement within the intrusion zone. The network device then evaluates the motion data against the applicable conditional settings. If the conditions are satisfied, the network device causes the security system to perform a designated action. For example, the system may activate an alarm, send a notification, begin recording, illuminate an area, or initiate another security response.
outputs.L4:
The application describes systems and methods for creating and managing conditional intrusion zones within a security environment. A network device stores configuration information defining one or more intrusion zones, a conditional setting associated with each zone, and a prescribed security action to be performed when the relevant conditions are met. The network device communicates with an audio/video recording and communication device, such as a security camera, video doorbell, or similar sensor-equipped device, and receives motion data representing activity detected within its field of view.

The received motion data is analyzed to determine whether detected movement occurred within a defined intrusion zone. The system also evaluates the associated conditional setting, which may account for contextual information such as the time of day, system mode, detected object type, occupancy status, or another specified criterion. If motion is detected within the intrusion zone and the conditional setting is satisfied, the network device initiates the prescribed security action. Such an action may include activating an alarm, generating a notification, beginning or extending an audio/video recording, illuminating an area, locking an entry point, or communicating with another security device or monitoring service.

By linking intrusion zones to configurable conditions and corresponding actions, the system can provide context-aware security responses rather than reacting identically to every motion event. This approach may reduce unnecessary alerts while allowing more urgent or appropriate actions to be taken when activity occurs under specified circumstances.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a system that creates intrusion zones for A/V recording and communication devices and triggers security actions when motion is detected and conditional settings are satisfied.
counterfactuals.output: A system and method for defining and monitoring intrusion zones associated with an audio/video recording and communication device are disclosed. The device captures image data representing an environment within a field of view. A user interface enables a user to designate one or more intrusion zones within the field of view and configure one or more conditional settings for each intrusion zone. A processor detects motion within the captured image data, determines whether the detected motion occurs within a designated intrusion zone, and evaluates whether the conditional settings are satisfied. The conditional settings may include temporal criteria, object classifications, motion characteristics, occupancy states, device states, user presence, or security-system modes. In response to determining that motion is detected within an intrusion zone and that the applicable conditional settings are satisfied, the system initiates one or more security actions. The security actions may include recording or storing audio/video data, transmitting a notification, establishing a communication session, activating an illumination or alarm device, locking an access point, or communicating with a monitoring service or another network-connected device. Different intrusion zones may be associated with different conditional settings and security actions, thereby enabling context-sensitive monitoring and response.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an example patent specification passage for conditional intrusion-zone monitoring in a networked home security system. Include motion detection and activation of an alarm.
counterfactuals.output:
### Example Patent Specification Passage

In one embodiment, a networked home security system includes a plurality of motion sensors positioned within respective intrusion zones of a premises, a security controller communicatively coupled to the motion sensors through a wired or wireless network, and one or more alarm devices. Each intrusion zone may be selectively placed in an active state, an inactive state, or a conditional monitoring state based on an operating mode of the security system, occupancy information, time of day, or the status of another zone or device.

When a first intrusion zone is in the conditional monitoring state, the security controller may disregard motion detected in the first intrusion zone unless a predefined activation condition is satisfied. For example, the activation condition may include detection of motion in an exterior entry zone, opening of a monitored door or window, absence of an authorized occupant, or expiration of an entry-delay period. Upon satisfaction of the activation condition, the security controller activates monitoring of the first intrusion zone for a selected duration.

If a motion sensor detects movement in the activated first intrusion zone, the motion sensor transmits a detection message to the security controller. The security controller evaluates the detection message according to an applicable alarm rule and, when the alarm rule is satisfied, generates an intrusion event. In response to the intrusion event, the security controller activates at least one alarm device, such as an audible siren, visual indicator, mobile-device notification, or remote monitoring notification. The controller may also cause one or more networked cameras to record or transmit image data associated with the first intrusion zone.

In some implementations, activation of the alarm may be suppressed or delayed when the detected motion corresponds to an authorized user, a recognized animal, or a scheduled occupancy condition. Thus, intrusion zones may be monitored conditionally to reduce false alarms while maintaining security coverage when predetermined risk conditions are present.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
